message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) belong to two different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, a group of placental mammals that split from other mammals roughly 90–100 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous. This ancestor would have been a small, generalized mammal that gave rise to the diverse lineages that eventually led to modern carnivores, odd‑toed ungulates (like zebras), even‑toed ungulates, bats, and cetaceans.
